'''Aditi Sen De''' (born 1 October 1974 in [[Kolkata]], India) is an Indian scientist<ref>{{cite web |title=Physicists prove impossible to mask quantum information |url=https://phys.org/news/2018-06-physicists-impossible-mask-quantum.html |website=Phys.org |publisher=Science X Network |date=12 June 2018 |access-date=28 February 2026 }}</ref>, a professor in [[quantum information]] and computation group at the [[Harish-Chandra Research Institute]], [[Prayagraj]]. She is known for her research on quantum information and computation, quantum communication including [[quantum cryptography]], [[quantum optics]] and many-body physics. The [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research]] awarded her the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize for Science and Technology]]<ref>{{cite web
 |title=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize (SSB) for Science and Technology 2018: Brief Profile of the Awardee
 |url=http://ssbprize.gov.in/Content/Detail.aspx?AID=545
 |publisher=Council of Scientific and Industrial Research
 |website=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize
 |date=1 October 2018
}}</ref> for her contributions to physical sciences in 2018. She is the first female physicist to be given this honour. In 2022, she was elected as a member of [[Indian Academy of Sciences]]<ref>{{cite web
 |title=Aditi Sen – Fellow Profile
 |url=https://fellows.ias.ac.in/profile/v/FL2022012
 |publisher=Indian Academy of Sciences
}}</ref> and [[Indian National Science Academy]]<ref>{{cite web
 |title=Newly elected members of INSA in 2022
 |url=https://insaindia.res.in/ref3.php
 |publisher=Indian National Science Academy
 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221022132711/https://www.insaindia.res.in/ref3.php
 |archive-date=22 October 2022
}}</ref>.

== Life and career ==

Aditi Sen De<ref>{{cite web
 |title='I Was the Only Woman in the Room': The Difficulty in Being a Female Scientist in India
 |url=https://www.news18.com/news/buzz/52016-thats-the-ratio-of-male-female-scientists-who-win-prizes-why-are-the-numbers-so-far-apart-2059227.html
 |website=News18
 |date=8 March 2019
}}</ref> was born in Kolkata, India to Lakshmi Dey and Ajit Kumar Dey. She did her schooling at Sarada Ashrama Balika Bidyalaya, Kolkata, and completed her higher secondary from [[Sakhawat Memorial Govt. Girls High School]], Kolkata in 1992. She joined [[Bethune College]], [[University of Calcutta]] to obtain a Bachelor of Science with honours in Mathematics. Subsequently, she joined the Applied Mathematics department of the [[Rajabazar Science College]], University of Calcutta. She received her master's degree in 1997, and after a short period of research<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Ghosh |first1=S. |last2=Kar |first2=G. |last3=Roy |first3=A. |last4=Sen(De) |first4=A. |last5=Sen |first5=U. |title=Distinguishability of Bell States |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=87 |issue=27 |article-number=277902 |year=2001 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.87.277902 |bibcode=2001PhRvL..87z7902G |url=https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.87.277902 |publisher=American Physical Society|arxiv=quant-ph/0106148 }}</ref><ref>{{cite arXiv |last1=Lewenstein |first1=Maciej |last2=Sanpera |first2=Anna |last3=Ahufinger |first3=Verónica |last4=Damski |first4=Bogdan |last5=Sen(De) |first5=Aditi |last6=Sen |first6=Ujjwal |title=Ultracold atomic gases in optical lattices: mimicking condensed matter physics and beyond |eprint=cond-mat/0606771 |year=2006 }}</ref> work in India, moved to [[Gdańsk]], [[Poland]] to work with [[Marek Żukowski]] at the [[University of Gdańsk]], where she received her PhD in January 2004.{{fact|date=February 2026}}

Following her doctoral studies she moved to [[Hannover]], [[Germany]] as a [[Alexander von Humboldt Foundation|Humboldt Research Fellow]]<ref>{{cite web
 |title=Prof. Dr. Aditi Sen De
 |url=https://www.humboldt-foundation.de/en/apply/sponsorship-programmes/feodor-lynen-research-fellowship/feodor-lynen-search-for-a-host/singleview?tx_rsmavhsolr_solrview%5BpPersonId%5D=1114346
 |publisher=Alexander von Humboldt Foundation
}}</ref> to work with [[Maciej Lewenstein]] at the [[Leibniz University]]. Thereafter, she joined [[ICFO - The Institute of Photonic Sciences]] at [[Barcelona]], [[Spain]]. She won the [[Ramón y Cajal (scholarship)|Ramón y Cajal research fellowship]] during her time in Spain.

Upon returning to [[India]] in 2008, she joined the School of Physical<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Sen(De) |first1=Aditi |last2=Sen |first2=Ujjwal |last3=Żukowski |first3=Marek |title=Quantum entanglement in multiparticle systems |journal=Physical Review A |volume=71 |issue=6 |article-number=062307 |year=2005 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevA.71.062307 |bibcode=2005PhRvA..71f2307S |url=https://journals.aps.org/pra/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevA.71.062307 |publisher=American Physical Society|arxiv=quant-ph/0410090 }}</ref> Sciences at [[Jawaharlal Nehru University]] as an Assistant Professor in Physics, before moving to [[Harish-Chandra Research Institute]], Allahabad in 2009, where she is currently a Professor in Physics. She has published more than 100 research articles<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Sen(De) |first1=Aditi |last2=Sen |first2=Ujjwal |last3=Żukowski |first3=Marek |title=Multiport quantum dense coding |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=90 |issue=10 |article-number=100402 |year=2003 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.90.100402 |bibcode=2003PhRvL..90j0402S |url=https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.90.100402 |publisher=American Physical Society|arxiv=quant-ph/0207168 }}</ref> in peer-reviewed journals.

She is married to fellow physicist Ujjwal Sen<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Ghosh |first1=Subhashish |last2=Kar |first2=Gour |last3=Roy |first3=Anirban |last4=Sen(De) |first4=Aditi |last5=Sen |first5=Ujjwal |title=Distinguishability of Bell States |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=93 |issue=21 |article-number=210501 |year=2004 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.93.210501 |bibcode=2004PhRvL..93u0501G |url=https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.93.210501 |publisher=American Physical Society|arxiv=quant-ph/0407037 }}</ref>, who is also a Professor of Physics at [[Harish-Chandra Research Institute]] in [[Allahabad]], [[India]]. They have a daughter, Anusyuta Sen.

== Research ==

Aditi Sen De started her research in the field of quantum information theory during her postgraduate studies in Kolkata and obtained her doctorate in 2004 at the [[University of Gdańsk]]. In collaboration with [[Marek Żukowski]], [[Ryszard Horodecki]], [[Paweł Horodecki]], [[Michał Horodecki]] and Ujjwal Sen, she worked on entanglement theory, quantum cryptography and quantum communication.{{fact|date=February 2026}}

She later worked with [[Maciej Lewenstein]] in Hannover and at [[ICFO - The Institute of Photonic Sciences]] near Barcelona. Her research includes quantum information, many-body quantum physics, [[quantum phase transition]]s using entanglement, [[quantum channel]]s, security of [[quantum cryptography]] and quantification of [[quantum correlation]]s.{{fact|date=February 2026}}

In 2009, she co-founded the Quantum Information and Computation group at [[Harish-Chandra Research Institute]] along with Ujjwal Sen and [[Arun K. Pati|Arun Kumar Pati]].{{fact|date=February 2026}}

== Awards and honours ==

In January 2022, she was elected to Indian Academy of Sciences. She was elected member of Indian National Science Academy in October 2022. The Council of Scientific and Industrial Research awarded her the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize]] in 2018. She is the first woman recipient of this Prize in the Physical Science category.

In 2012, she won the Buti Foundation Award. She has also received the Ramón y Cajal fellowship in Spain and the Humboldt Research Fellowship given by the [[Alexander von Humboldt Foundation]] in Germany.
